findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-07-27) the CFO set a Q3 NIM 'launch point' of about 3.44-3.45% against the 3.38% reported for Q2 (June alone 3.48%), said 'a major portion of that can persist', and expects ~20 bp of monthly loan-yield benefit a year out; at 3.45% that is roughly +$0.6-0.9M of NII on Q2's $30.8M, which is about what a $0.57-0.58 consensus needs once the guided slightly higher Q3 salaries and the absence of Q2's $320K provision reversal are netted out.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NIM +14 bp with EPS $0.58 vs $0.52 consensus: stock +5.32% on the day (baseline, 2026-07-27). Q1 2026, an EPS miss: -2.20% (2026-04-27). The name has paid for margin expansion beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the launch point is the company's own public statement, and consensus at $0.57 (below Q2's $0.58) already reflects flat earnings. What is not in the price is a NIM above ~3.47%; if the market expected that, consensus would sit above $0.60.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K exhibit 99.1 documents the 3.38% NIM, 1.28% deposit cost and 6.53% new-loan yield the guide builds on: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001403475/000140347526000035/earningsrelease-ex991q22026.htm (same company, different document).

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25 bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0), after management's Q2 remarks were made; for a bank with 36.7% non-interest-bearing deposits, no short-term borrowings and management saying it sees 'no real upward pressure' on deposit rates, prime-linked loan repricing should lift the Q4 NIM outlook beyond the 3.44-3.45% launch point, the forward line the call will be asked about.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior rate-hike quarter in the 7-print baseline; the closest is Q2 2026, when margin expansion commentary went with +5.32%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced in sector multiples, but BMRC has no option chain and three to five analysts, and its Q3 consensus at $0.57 does not extrapolate the hike into the quarter's exit NIM; if the street had marked BMRC's asset sensitivity up, estimates would have moved above Q2's $0.58. The 10-Q's rate sensitivity table was not read, so the sign of BMRC's sensitivity is not confirmed by the company: this is macro-to-company transmission.
findings.independence: Proxy. The direct counterparty evidence is the Q2 call remark that deposit-rate pressure is absent (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2937974); also Westamerica's Q3 cost of funds rose only 2 bp to 0.26% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000311094/000117184326006660/exh_991.htm).

findings.finding: Two California community banks that reported Q3 2026 after BMRC last spoke showed wider margins and benign credit: Westamerica (2026-10-15) NIM 3.81%, +4 bp QoQ, deposits +0.9% QoQ, zero provision, nonperforming loans 0.07%; Community West Bancshares (2026-10-22) NIM 4.65%, +9 bp, cost of deposits 1.27%, down 4 bp, provision $0.58M vs $5.6M in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No peer-read history for this name; BMRC's own credit-clean, margin-up quarters (Q2 2026, Q4 2025) were +5.32% and +3.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer prints are public, and BMRC rose 3.26% over the five sessions they landed in, which may be the price absorbing them; the remaining value is that neither peer showed the deposit outflow or CRE migration that would be the bear case for a Marin/Sonoma lender. Westamerica's loan book fell 1.6% QoQ, so loan growth is not corroborated.
findings.independence: Second, independent peer: Westamerica Q3 2026 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000311094/000117184326006660/exh_991.htm (2026-10-15). Both are proxies for BMRC, not BMRC numbers.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 22% in the second half of September to 1,056,460 shares (about 6.5% of shares outstanding) at the 2026-09-30 settlement, from 865,943 on 09-15 and 839,638 on 07-15, with 5.4 days to cover on ~118k shares a day; a clean print meets a short base that is building into it and needs five-plus sessions to exit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of seven prints up, two of them more than +5% (+5.32% 2026-07-27, +5.63% 2025-01-27), on similar short levels (days to cover 4.9-5.9 over the summer).
findings.why_not_priced: The building short is itself a bet that something negative is coming, which cuts both ways; what is not priced is the asymmetry of a 5-7 day cover on a thin name if the print is clean. If shorts had already covered, the 10-15 settlement (published only on 10-26) would show it.
findings.independence: finviz shows short float 6.84%, short ratio 7.13: https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=BMRC (same FINRA data, different aggregator, so one fact).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-16 the head of retail banking, EVP Brandi Campbell, left by 'mutual agreement' with three months' severance and no successor named (8-K item 5.02), forfeiting 18,069 restricted shares (Form 4, 2026-10-19); retail banking runs the branch deposit franchise behind a Q2 deposit fall of $58.2M (1.7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a week, and the stock rose 3.26% over it, so largely priced; what is left is whether the call links the departure to Q3 deposit performance. The forfeiture is a small Q4 expense credit, outside the quarter being reported.

findings.finding: Capital return is unlikely to surprise: Bancorp CET1 12.93% and TCE 8.52% at 2026-06-30 with $23.9M of its $25M buyback authorization unused, but management said on the Q2 call 'I wouldn't call any buybacks imminent' and noted dividends need California regulator approval after the restructuring losses; the $0.25 quarterly dividend is normally declared alongside the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback or dividend change in the baseline window; 85 consecutive quarterly dividends.
findings.why_not_priced: The no-buyback stance is public, so a buyback restart would be the only unpriced item and it is unlikely; a dividend cut would show up as a negative skew, and there is no chain to show one.
findings.independence: Q2 call remarks on buybacks and regulator approval: https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2937974.

Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the buyback finding's own text says management called buybacks not imminent, so +0.1 went to +0.05.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): two estimate sources agree at $0.57-0.58, so no cap was applied; Benzinga's revenue bar was disowned in `bar` rather than used.
